item.title: Thoracolumbar Fascial MFR
clinicalUse: Perceived lumbar stiffness/myofascial pain as an adjunct
patientPosition: Prone with abdomen supported if needed.
contact: Cross-hand or broad palm contact over thoracolumbar fascia, avoiding direct painful pressure on spinous processes.
forceDirection: Slow longitudinal/diagonal load toward restriction or direction of ease.
mistakes: Very deep pressure in acute pain.
Claiming fascia has been permanently released.
safety: Avoid over acute fracture, infection, open wound or suspected serious pathology.
item.visualCue: Cross-hand thoracolumbar contact → Slow sustained load → Active re-test.

subTechniques.name: Thoracolumbar Fascial Release
subTechniques.target: Thoracolumbar fascia and lumbar paraspinal interface
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce painful guarding and improve tolerance to lumbar flexion/rotation when soft-tissue restriction is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone or side-lying with the abdomen/pelvis supported for comfort.
subTechniques.contact: Broad crossed-hand or parallel-hand contact over the lumbar/thoracolumbar fascia.
subTechniques.direction: Take up skin/fascial slack slowly and sustain the load in the most restricted direction; avoid heavy downward compression.
subTechniques.reassess: Lumbar flexion/rotation and the patient's bending or sit-to-stand task.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: The technique should feel like a slow tissue load, not a deep massage.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Do not use routine manual treatment when serious spinal pathology is suspected.
